I have tried several reusable K-Cups and these are one of the best.  Other brands I have tried have had problems such as letting too much of the fine coffee grounds get into the coffee cup (screen not fine enough), and one brand was directional but had mesh screen on a flat bottom so I accidentally punched a hole in it. One brand's lid broke off after a few uses.  The STK's seem to have strong lid hinges and the mesh screen is fine so it gives me a great cup of coffee.  The lids have an O-ring letting the lid snap down tight.  It is directional but if you do happen to put it in wrong, you won't be punching a hole in the bottom because there is plastic (not mesh screen) that will prevent that accident.  I would recommend this brand.

I ordered these because they fit into my MR Coffee Keurig maker. For my main Keurig maker, I use another product with a gold filter, so I had something to compare to. The coffee made with this filter came out sludgy with poor taste. Also, in order to fit the maker, the bottom portion is indented, and it makes it very hard to clean the coffee out. You have to used your finger or the edge of a spoon to stir up the coffee. My other filter just washes right out with the faucet. My biggest concern is this design. Instead of the filters being full filter around the sides of the cup, there is intervening plastic. I do not understand this design, and when looking for a replacement I noted many other ones for sale also have this design. With this design boiling hot coffee filters and then runs over plastic before exiting the unit. After a little while, I noticed that the plastic is placed in such a way to create a design out of the filter -  2 dolphins swimming!!!  Do we really need a dolphin design to make a cup of coffee, how about maximizing the filtering area to produce a better cup of coffee. I have had to return and will try another design with a full filter. I do not recommend this product.

It states unequivocally that this filter is a comparable replacement for the Whirlpool 4396841, 4396710, and W10193691 but with superior performance. Also it is claimed that the piece was designed with usability in mind, this filter is packaged with louder colors and an instinctive model number to practically guarantee you are getting the right filter for your fridge. Along with this comes a significant increase in contaminant reduction up from 16 to a NSF certified 66. Now, my issue comes in the fact that aside from the astronomical price, the filter (which does everything but give you a sponge bath) needs to have three gallons of water flushed through it in order to be safe and drinkable.  I don't know about you, but in order to complete this requisite requirement, one is spending an inordinate amount of time filling and dumping out 'fresh' water from the fridge dispenser. Given this initial task, three stars seems more than generous.
